--- PART 1/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Parent's high fitness suggests it plays well against peers." / "Given parent is already best, maybe we should avoid risky probes and just take safe improvements"
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like strategy that cooperates when opponent never defected, defects when opponent never cooperated, retaliates after repeated defections, and has a final-round defect check that never fires. The trace simulates matches against listed peers (always-D, TFT, forgiving TFT, random-ish, complex) and archive possibilities (all-C, grim trigger). It proposes changes: defect on the actual final round (n==99), possibly probe/exploit never-defecting opponents, and avoid risky early probes against possible grim triggers.

--- PART 2/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report / "Given the lack of information, the safest improvement is to fix the final round and maybe improve forgiveness logic." / "Given the uncertainty, I think the safest improvement is to take parent's code and: - Fix final round: if n == 99: return D."
STRATEGY: Parent is a TFT-like IPD strategy with heuristics for high cooperation, opponent defection runs, and a random near-end probe; the trace simulates it against pseudo-random, always-D, always-C, TFT, grim, and forgiving opponents; proposed changes are fixing the final-round defect from n==100 to n==99, removing or limiting the random near-end probe, and adding a single late probe against never-defecting opponents.

--- PART 3/3 ---
ORIGIN: NONE
CONTRADICTION: NONE
RESOLUTION: kept using the report — "Parent's fitness might have been slightly higher with it if all-C was common, but we don't know. Given that parent was best, maybe the random probe helped."
STRATEGY: Parent cooperates when opponent has never defected, defects on final round, retaliates/forgives based on opponent's last moves, and randomly probes late against high-cooperation opponents. The trace simulates this against TFT, all-C, and grim, then changes the strategy by adding a deterministic final-round defect and removing the random late probe.
